title: When Metrics Become Targets
equation: Measure Validity = 1 ÷ Pressure to Hit It
hook: The second you tie a bonus to a number, people start gaming the number.
statement: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.
explainer: Measure support on tickets closed per hour and tickets get closed without being solved. People chase whatever's counted. Pair every target with a second number that catches the gaming.
sop: List the metrics your team is chasing.
For each, write how someone could game it.
Add a balancing metric next to it.
Watch for weird behavior around the number.
Fix or replace any metric that's been gamed.
equation_example: Pressure to Hit It is 9 out of 10, tied to bonuses. Measure Validity = 1 ÷ 9, about 0.11 out of 1.0. More pressure pushes validity toward zero. Low pressure, around 1 or 2, keeps the number closer to reality.
question: Pick one metric your team is rewarded on and write the easiest way to game it.
closing_statement: The moment you reward a number, people optimize the number.
caption:
Principle Nº 316: When Metrics Become Targets

The second you tie a bonus to a number, people start gaming the number.

When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.

Your turn: Pick one metric your team is rewarded on and write the easiest way to game it.
